format.description: Always `"wmxdsl-resolved"`. Lets a consumer reject a file that is not a Resolved Document before reading further.

version.description: Format major version. Bumped on any change that removes a field, changes a field's type or meaning, or weakens a guarantee in the schema document. Adding a field does not bump it.

meta.description: Frontmatter metadata, with defaults written in (spec §04).

breakpoints.description: Sorted, total cover of all viewport widths from 0 upward, each range naming the variant it selects (spec §07.4). The active variant is the last entry whose `minWidth` is at or below the viewport width.

fonts.description: Every registered font face, from theme and document (spec §07.1). Layout waits for the faces its active scenes use.

strings.description: All text of the document, once. Runs, drop caps and end marks refer to entries by index. Quotes are curled, dashes and ellipses substituted, and U+00AD soft hyphens inserted (spec §10.2, §15.4 point 4).

propertyNames.description: Asset id. Opaque, stable within one build, unique in `assets`.

assets.description: Media files, generated responsive sets, text tracks and traced polygons, keyed by asset id. Shared by all variants so art-directed and repeated media is stored once (spec §11.4-§11.9, §12.2).

variants.description: One complete variant per breakpoint plus `base` (spec §06.4). Nothing in a variant falls back to another variant.

music.description: Soundtrack cues in document order (spec §10.6). The playing track is the last cue above the reading position. Empty when the document has none.

diagnostics.description: Resolve and asset warnings (errors fail the build and never reach here). Carried for tooling and for the runtime console; layout ignores them (spec §15.6).

ResolvedDocument.description: The resolver's entire output and the layout engine's entire input (spec §15.1, §15.3). Every value is concrete: no tokens, `extends`, `parent`, defaults, shorthand or viewport-dependent result remains.

wmxdsl.description: Language major version from frontmatter `wmxdsl`. Always 1 (spec §17).

title.description: Document title for `<title>` and social cards. Independent of `\headline` (spec §04).

lang.description: BCP-47 language tag; `"en"` when the frontmatter sets none. Drives quote curling, hyphenation and the page's `lang` (spec §04, §10.2).

authors.description: Author names from frontmatter `author`, a single string becoming a one-element list; `[]` when absent. Metadata only; the visible byline is a `\byline` (spec §04).

date.description: ISO 8601 date string exactly as given, or `null` (spec §04).

socialImage.description: Social card image, as an image asset id, or `null` (spec §04).

theme.description: Theme file path as written in frontmatter, or `null`. Provenance only: its definitions are already applied (spec §07.8).

Meta.description: Frontmatter, resolved (spec §04). Absent optional fields are written as `null` or `[]`, never omitted.

AssetId.description: Asset id. Opaque, stable within one build, unique in `assets`.

minWidth.description: Lowest viewport width, in CSS px, inclusive, that selects `variant`. The first entry is always 0.

variant.description: Key into `variants`. The same name may appear twice when a named breakpoint splits `base` into two ranges.

BreakpointRange.description: One threshold of the breakpoint cover. Ranges are half-open: this one runs from `minWidth` up to the next entry's `minWidth`.

VariantName.description: Variant name: `"base"` or the name of a `\breakpoint` (spec §07.4).

family.description: Family name exactly as styles refer to it.

src.description: Public URL of the font file, as the build emits it.

weight.description: Weight range the file covers. A static face has `min` equal to `max`; a variable face such as `300-700` has both ends (spec §07.1).

Asset.description: A file the page loads, or data the build derived from one.

width.description: Intrinsic width of the source image in px.

height.description: Intrinsic height of the source image in px.

animated.description: True for an animated image such as a GIF (spec §11.4).

ImageAsset.description: An image and its generated responsive set (spec §11.4).

MediaSource.description: One encoding of a video or audio file.

url.description: Public URL of the `.json` or `.lottie` file.

width.description: Width in px, from the file.

height.description: Height in px, from the file.

FileAsset.description: A file used as-is: a `.vtt` caption track or a transcript (spec §11.5, §11.8).

points.description: Vertices in order, at least three.

PolygonAsset.description: A polygon in normalized box coordinates, `[0, 0]` top-left to `[1, 1]` bottom-right. Layout scales it to the object's box and expands it by `wrap-offset` (spec §12.2).

base.description: The variant for every width no named breakpoint covers (spec §07.4).

Variants.description: The variants, keyed by name. `base` is always present, and so is every breakpoint named in `breakpoints`.

propertyNames.description: Style key: an author or theme style name for a block style, or a composed key for a run style (see `ResolvedStyle`).

styles.description: Every style key referenced anywhere in this variant, fully flattened. Contains exactly the referenced keys (spec §07.6).

propertyNames.description: Story id: the `\story` name, or `<ownerId>#text` for an inline frame, pull quote or sidebar, `<ownerId>#caption` for a caption and credit, `folio#text` for the document's folio, `<parentName>#folio` for a parent's.

stories.description: Every story, named and anonymous. A named story has the same block list, in the same order, in every variant.

scenes.description: Scenes in document order, parents already merged in (spec §08, §08.4).

propertyNames.description: Frame id: author `name`, else `frame-<n>` in document order; `<sceneId>/<id>` for a frame instantiated from a parent; `<sceneId>/frame` for the default frame of a shorthand or implicit scene.

frames.description: Every frame in the document, hidden ones included, keyed by id (spec §09.2).

propertyNames.description: Object id: author `name`, else `<command>-<n>` numbered per command in document order (`figure-2`); `<sceneId>/<id>` when instantiated from a parent. Groups, scene-level rules and gallery children are objects.

objects.description: Every object, grid-placed, anchored, background, grouped and gallery children, hidden ones included, keyed by id (spec §11).

propertyNames.description: Story id: the `\story` name, or `<ownerId>#text` for an inline frame, pull quote or sidebar, `<ownerId>#caption` for a caption and credit, `folio#text` for the document's folio, `<parentName>#folio` for a parent's.

threads.description: For each story shown in frames, its visible frames in thread order: scene order, then source order in the scene, hidden frames removed (spec §09.3). Stories laid out by an object, such as captions, are not listed.

Variant.description: Everything layout and the renderer need for one breakpoint, fully valued.

family.description: Font family fallback list, most preferred first; generic families such as `serif` are allowed (spec §07.1, §07.6).

size.description: Font size: `px` or `fluid` (spec §07.6). For a composed run style, already scaled against its block style.

leading.description: Line height. `bl` means baseline steps of the scene grid the line lands in (spec §07.6).

tracking.description: Letter spacing, `em` already multiplied out against `size` (spec §07.6).

case.description: Case transform applied to the text before measuring and rendering (spec §07.6).

align.description: Horizontal alignment within the slot (spec §07.6). `justify` spreads a line to the slot's full width by widening its spaces; the line that ends a paragraph is left alone.

underline.description: True when the text is underlined. Only the composed `+link` styles set it, from the default theme's link style (spec §16).

indent.description: First-line indent the style asks for. The indent actually applied to a paragraph is `ParagraphBlock.indent` (spec §07.6).

spaceBefore.description: Space above the block, suppressed at the top of a frame or column (spec §07.6).

hyphenate.description: Whether the U+00AD soft hyphens in this style's text are honoured. When false, the consumer strips them before prepare (spec §07.6).

widows.description: Minimum lines of a paragraph at the top of a frame or column (spec §07.6).

orphans.description: Minimum lines of a paragraph at the bottom of a frame or column (spec §07.6).

keepWithNext.description: Keep this block in the same frame or column as the next block (spec §07.6).

balance.description: Break lines evenly: at the narrowest width that takes no more lines than the slot's (spec §07.6).

hyphenMark.description: `both`: a hyphenated word also shows a hyphen where it continues, hanging before the next line (spec §07.6).

composer.description: `paragraph`: each line's break is chosen for the whole paragraph, evening the spacing and keeping a word from standing alone on the last line; `line`: each line takes as many words as fit (spec §07.6).

hyphenateMin.description: The shortest word, in letters, that hyphenates (spec §07.6).

hyphenateCaps.description: False: a word that starts with a capital never hyphenates (spec §07.6).

hang.description: Quotation marks (`quotes`), and also hyphens, full stops and commas (`punctuation`), at a line's edge hang outside the column (spec §07.6).

bindShort.description: A short word (a, the, of, to...) never ends a line: it stays with the word after it (spec §07.6).

justifyMin.description: With `align=justify`, a line in a slot narrower than this is set ragged right instead; `null`: every line justifies (spec §07.6).

minSlot.description: The narrowest gap beside an object that text is set in; a narrower gap stays empty (spec §07.6, §09.6 step 3). `null`: 6em of the style's size, whatever size it ends with.

mark.description: A pull quote's decorative mark, such as `“`, set above its text at three times the size, bold, in the accent; `null` for none (spec §07.6).

features.description: OpenType feature tags to enable, for example `["liga", "kern", "onum"]` (spec §07.6).

snap.description: `baseline`: each line's baseline sits on the grid step. `none`: lines use their own leading and the block's height rounds up to whole baseline steps (spec §07.6).

fit.description: `fit=width`: set each paragraph at the largest size, from `size` to `max` (three times `size` when `null`), that splits no word and, with `height`, stays no taller (spec §07.6). `null` for `fit=none`.

ResolvedStyle.description: A fully flattened paragraph or run style (spec §07.6). Block keys are style names. Run keys are composed as `<blockKey>` then, in this order and only if present, `+strong`, `+em`, `+code`, `+link`, then `+span:<name>` per `\span` from outermost to innermost: `body+em+link`, `headline+span:smallcaps`.

Len.description: A length whose value needs at most the viewport or the frame's scene grid. `rem`, `em`, tokens, and `bl` inside grid definitions are already eliminated (spec §06.3).

n.description: Percent of the viewport dimension: 40 means 40vw.

LenViewport.description: A fraction of the viewport: `vw` of its width, `vh` of the small viewport height (spec §06.3).

n.description: Percent: 50 means half the reference box.

LenPct.description: A percentage of the reference box the field's own description names (spec §06.3).

n.description: Number of columns or baseline steps.

LenGrid.description: Grid-relative: `col` is n columns including the n-1 gutters between them, `bl` is n baseline steps, both of the grid of the scene where the element is laid out (spec §06.3).

min.description: Pixels at or below viewport width `from`.

max.description: Pixels at or above viewport width `to`.

from.description: Viewport width in px where interpolation starts.

to.description: Viewport width in px where interpolation ends.

LenFluid.description: Linear from `min` px at viewport width `from` to `max` px at `to`, clamped outside that range (spec §06.3).

Color.description: A color: a palette role, resolved against the palette of the scene the element is rendered in, or a fixed hex value (spec §07.3).

role.description: One of the five fixed roles.

ColorRole.description: A palette role, left symbolic so a scene's palette restyles everything in it (spec §07.3).

hex.description: Eight lowercase hex digits with a leading `#`, alpha last: `#e0563aff`.

max.description: Largest size, or `null` for three times the style's size.

height.description: Tallest the paragraph may be, or `null` for no limit.

origin.description: Where the story came from. `named` is a `\story`; the others are anonymous stories owned by `owner` (spec §09.2, §11.10).

owner.description: The frame or object that owns an anonymous story, or `null` for a named story and the folio.

overset.description: What happens to text left over after the last frame of the thread is full (spec §09.5). Anonymous stories are always `grow`.

blocks.description: The content, in source order. A thread cursor addresses a block by its index here (spec §09.1).

Story.description: A run of content with no position of its own (spec §09.1).

StoryId.description: Story id: the `\story` name, or `<ownerId>#text` for an inline frame, pull quote or sidebar, `<ownerId>#caption` for a caption and credit, `folio#text` for the document's folio, `<parentName>#folio` for a parent's.

FrameId.description: Frame id: author `name`, else `frame-<n>` in document order; `<sceneId>/<id>` for a frame instantiated from a parent; `<sceneId>/frame` for the default frame of a shorthand or implicit scene.

ObjectId.description: Object id: author `name`, else `<command>-<n>` numbered per command in document order (`figure-2`); `<sceneId>/<id>` when instantiated from a parent. Groups, scene-level rules and gallery children are objects.

Block.description: One unit of story content. Anchored objects, frame breaks and in-frame rules are blocks, so every anchor falls between blocks.

element.description: The source construct, which the renderer maps to an HTML element: `prose` is bare prose, the rest are the text commands of spec §10.3.

level.description: Heading level for `subhead` (1 or 2, rendered `h2`/`h3`); `null` for every other element (spec §10.3).

quote.description: Consecutive blocks with the same number belong to one `\blockquote`, counted from 1 within the story; `null` outside a block quote (spec §10.3).

style.description: Block style key, and the value of `style` on every Positioned Line of this paragraph (spec §07.6, §15.3).

span.description: `all` stretches the block across every internal column of a multi-column frame; `column` is the normal case (spec §10.3).

indent.description: First-line indent actually applied: the style's indent, or zero `px` where §07.6 says it is skipped (first paragraph of a story, after a non-paragraph block, under a drop cap).

dropcap.description: The drop cap on this paragraph, or `null` (spec §10.4).

runs.description: The paragraph's content as a flat list of styled runs. When there is a drop cap, the runs start after the cap's graphemes.

links.description: Link targets. A text run's `link` indexes this list, so consecutive runs with the same index form one link (spec §10.2).

ParagraphBlock.description: A paragraph of text: bare prose or a text element (spec §10.1, §10.3).

StyleKey.description: Style key: an author or theme style name for a block style, or a composed key for a run style (see `ResolvedStyle`).

chars.description: Graphemes taken, not counting an opening quotation mark (spec §10.4 `chars`).

s.description: The exact cap text, including any opening quotation mark, as a string index. The paragraph's runs do not repeat it.

style.description: Style key of the cap, normally `dropcap` (spec §10.4, §16).

hang.description: True when the cap's opening quotation mark hangs outside the column, so the letter lines up with the text (spec §10.4 `quote=hang`).

Dropcap.description: A drop cap: the inputs to measuring and placing it. Its width is measured during prepare and lives on the prepared paragraph, not here (spec §10.4).

s.description: The text, as a string index.

style.description: Composed run style key: what the text engine measures with.

marks.description: Semantic marks, outermost first, for `<strong>`, `<em>` and `<code>`. Independent of appearance (spec §10.2).

link.description: Index into the paragraph's `links`, or `null` when the run is not in a link.

TextRun.description: Text in one style with one set of semantics.

s.description: The glyph, as a string index.

style.description: Composed style key `<paragraph style>+endmark`: the enclosing paragraph's style in the accent color.

href.description: The URL as written, relative paths resolved against the source file.

object.description: The anchored object. Present in `objects` even when hidden; a hidden object is stepped over.

ObjectBlock.description: An anchored object's position in its story. Layout places the object when the flow reaches this block (spec §11.3).

scope.description: `frame` ends the frame and all its remaining columns; `column` ends only the current internal column (spec §09.3).

RuleBlock.description: A `\rule` inside a frame: a horizontal divider set as a block (spec §10.4).

width.description: Length of the line; `pct` is of the column or box it sits in.

align.description: Where a rule shorter than its column sits.

parent.description: Name of the parent this scene was built from, or `null`. Provenance only: attributes and children are already merged (spec §08.4).

grid.description: The scene's grid at this breakpoint (spec §07.5).

palette.description: The scene's palette at this breakpoint, all five roles concrete (spec §07.3).

height.description: `flow`: as tall as its content plus `margin-y`. `screen`: one small-viewport height, divided into rows. `page`: at least one small-viewport height, taller when its content needs it; multi-column frames fill column bands (spec §08.2, §09.7).

snap.description: Scroll snapping on the scene's top edge. `hard` on a flow scene is already downgraded to `soft` (spec §08.3).

turn.description: How the page arrives when the reader reaches it, or `null` for none (spec §08.3).

linearized.description: True when this scene linearized at this breakpoint. Placements below are already rewritten: stacked in source order at full width, one internal column, wrap `jump` (spec §07.5).

folio.description: The folio shown while this scene is under it: the scene's parent's folio if it declares one, else the document's; `null` when there is none or the scene sets `folio=hide` (spec §10.5).

children.description: Top-level children in paint order: the parent's children first, beneath, then the scene's own, each in source order (spec §08.4, §11.3). Anchored objects are not listed here; they belong to their story.

Scene.description: A full-width band of the article (spec §08.1).

SceneId.description: Scene id: the scene's `name`, else `scene-1`, `scene-2`... in document order (spec §08.1). Also the scene's element id and URL fragment.

marginY.description: Top and bottom scene padding; `bl` already converted to px.

max.description: Maximum width of the column area; beyond it the grid centers and the margins grow.

baseline.description: Baseline step in px: the `bl` unit for everything in this scene.

rows.description: Row count, used only by screen scenes (spec §08.2).

body.description: Columns of the default frame, with `all` resolved (spec §07.5 `body`).

outdent.description: How far an object on the grid's left or right outer edge reaches into the margin (spec §07.5 `outdent`).

Grid.description: A grid's inputs at one breakpoint. Layout computes geometry from these and the viewport width (spec §07.5).

TrackRange.description: A grid track range, 1-based and inclusive, with `end` and `all` already resolved to numbers (spec §06.2).

accent.description: Kickers, links, drop caps, pull quote marks.

Palette.description: The five palette roles as hex colors (spec §07.3).

effect.description: `fade`, or `slide`: 8% of the viewport height into place while fading, from the scroll direction.

SceneTurn.description: A page turn (spec §08.3): plays each time the scene enters the viewport after being fully out of it.

story.description: Its text as an anonymous story: `folio#text` for the document's folio, `<parentName>#folio` for a parent's.

progress.description: Show a reading-progress indicator for the whole article.

Folio.description: The persistent label fixed to the viewport (spec §10.5).

kind.description: Which table the id is in.

ElementRef.description: A reference to a frame or an object (groups are objects).

id.description: Frame id, and the `frame` of every Positioned Line set in it.

story.description: The story shown. For an inline frame this is its anonymous story, `<id>#text` (spec §09.2).

cols.description: Columns spanned, with the grid's `body` default and linearize already applied.

columns.description: Number of internal columns (spec §09.2 `columns`). `auto` leaves the number to layout, which fits the columns to `measure` -- or, with no measure, to 32 times the text size -- so a wider screen gets more columns rather than longer lines.

balance.description: Balance internal columns when the frame has no definite height (spec §09.4).

columnRule.description: `rule`: a 1px line in the palette's `rule` colour mid-gap between columns that hold text, per band (spec §09.2).

valign.description: Vertical alignment of content that fits a definite height (spec §09.2).

measure.description: Cap on every line's width, including lines beside a wrap; the capped slot stays left-aligned. `null` means no cap (spec §09.2 `measure`).

z.description: Stacking order within the content layer, source order written in (spec §09.2).

hidden.description: True when hidden at this breakpoint. A hidden frame is absent from `threads` (spec §09.3).

wrap.description: `wrap=rect` (spec §09.2): the frame's box, to its last line, cuts into the frames set after it, as an object's rectangle does, with `offset` below it (not at its sides, which are on grid lines). `null` for `wrap=none`.

Frame.description: A rectangle on a scene's grid that shows a slice of a story (spec §09.2).

Vertical.description: Vertical placement on the grid. Which shape applies depends on the scene's height mode (spec §08.2).

top.description: Offset from the top of the scene's content area, or `auto`: below the previous sibling in source order that overlaps its columns, separated by `row-gap` (spec §09.2).

height.description: Box height, or `auto`: from the content, or from `ratio` for media (spec §09.2, §11.1).

VerticalFlow.description: Vertical placement in a flow scene (spec §09.2 `top`, `height`).

VerticalRows.description: Vertical placement in a screen scene: a range of the grid's rows (spec §08.2).

enter.description: Animation as the element enters the viewport.

exit.description: Animation as the element leaves through the top of the viewport.

enterAt.description: Fraction of the element that must be inside the viewport before `enter` fires: 0.15 is `15%`.

delayMs.description: Delay in milliseconds, including this element's stagger step.

replay.description: Replay `enter` every time the element comes back into view.

motion.description: `reduce`: every reveal becomes `none` under reduced motion. `always`: this element keeps its motion (spec §13 rule 3).

Reveal.description: Reveal animation parameters, with any scene, parent or group stagger already baked into `delayMs` (spec §13).

kind.description: Object kind, and the Positioned Object's `kind`.

image.description: Image asset for this breakpoint; `src@phone` selects a different one (spec §11.4).

motionVideo.description: For an animated GIF the compiler transcoded, the looping muted video asset; otherwise `null` (spec §11.4).

alt.description: Text alternative. `""` marks a decorative image; `null` means missing, which warned (spec §11.4).

id.description: Object id, and the `name` of its Positioned Object.

layer.description: Paint layer. Only `content` can exclude text (spec §11.2).

z.description: Stacking order within the layer, source order written in (spec §11.1).

bleed.description: Sides on which the box extends through the margin to the viewport edge (spec §11.1).

maxWidth.description: Cap on the box width, or `null` for none. The box keeps the centre of the space its placement gave it, so the room it gives back is shared by the text on both sides (spec §11.1).

offsetX.description: Horizontal fine adjustment of the box (spec §11.1).

offsetY.description: Vertical fine adjustment of the box (spec §11.1).

wrap.description: How text flows around the object. Always `none` off the content layer (spec §12).

hidden.description: True when hidden at this breakpoint. An anchored hidden object is stepped over by layout (spec §09.3, §11.1).

ratio.description: Box aspect ratio, `auto` already replaced by the media's own (spec §11.4).

fit.description: How the media fills the box.

focus.description: Focal point kept in view when `cover` crops.

shape.description: The object's outline (spec §12.2). `rect` when the command takes no `shape`.

MediaFit.description: How visual media fill their box (spec §11.4).

Ratio.description: An aspect ratio, width to height. `auto` is already replaced by the media's intrinsic ratio (spec §06.2, §11.4).

x.description: 0 is the left edge, 1 the right.

y.description: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom.

FocusPoint.description: A point inside a box, in fractions from the top-left: `x: 0.5, y: 0.7` is `"50% 70%"` (spec §11.4 `focus`).

Shape.description: An object's outline, used for contour wrap and for clipping (spec §12.2).

ShapeInscribed.description: A circle or an ellipse inscribed in the box (spec §12.2).

polygon.description: A `polygon` asset in normalized box coordinates.

source.description: Where the polygon came from. Provenance only.

ShapePolygon.description: A polygon: from `poly(...)`, or traced from the alpha channel at build time with `fit`/`focus` crops applied first (spec §12.2).

story.description: Anonymous story holding the `\caption` and `\credit` paragraphs, `<ownerId>#caption`.

side.description: Where it sits. `overlay` takes no space in the box (spec §11.1).

Placement.description: Where an object's position comes from (spec §11.3).

GridPlacement.description: Grid-placed: written directly in a scene (spec §11.3).

block.description: Index of the anchor's `ObjectBlock` in that story's `blocks`.

height.description: Box height, or `auto` from ratio or content (spec §11.1).

AnchoredPlacement.description: Anchored: written in a story, so it travels with the text (spec §11.3).

AnchorHorizontal.description: Horizontal position of an anchored object (spec §11.3).

AnchorFull.description: `side=full` (the default): the full width of the current frame column; text stops above and resumes below.

side.description: Which edge of the column the object sits against; `center`: centred in it, text on both sides (2026-10-09).

width.description: Object width; `pct` is of the column width.

AnchorSide.description: `side=left` or `right` with a width: inside the current column, and text wraps beside it.

AnchorCols.description: `cols=`: absolute grid columns of the scene the anchor lands in, whichever frame holds it. Text in any overlapping frame wraps.

BackgroundPlacement.description: `layer=background`: fills the whole scene behind everything; `cols`, `rows` and `top` do not apply (spec §11.2).

index.description: Position among the container's children, from 0.

ContainedPlacement.description: Inside a group or gallery, which positions its children itself; the child's own placement attributes are ignored (spec §11.9, §11.11).

Wrap.description: How text flows around an object (spec §12.1).

WrapNone.description: Text ignores the object and may overlap it.

offset.description: Standoff above and below the object (spec §12.1 `wrap-offset`).

WrapJump.description: Text skips the object's full vertical extent.

mode.description: Wrap tag. `contour` with a `rect` shape behaves like `rect`.

side.description: Which side or sides of the object text may occupy; `both` sets text in two slots per band (spec §12.1).

offset.description: Standoff between the exclusion and the text (spec §12.1).

WrapShaped.description: Text is cut by an exclusion: the box for `rect`, the object's `shape` for `contour` (spec §12.1, §12.2).

poster.description: Poster image asset, or `null` when missing (warned unless background) (spec §11.5).

play.description: `visible` plays only while in the viewport. Becomes `manual` under reduced motion at runtime (spec §11.5, §13).

controls.description: Show controls; `false` by default on the background layer (spec §11.5).

id.description: Object id, and the `name` of its Positioned Object.

layer.description: Paint layer. Only `content` can exclude text (spec §11.2).

z.description: Stacking order within the layer, source order written in (spec §11.1).

bleed.description: Sides on which the box extends through the margin to the viewport edge (spec §11.1).

maxWidth.description: Cap on the box width, or `null` for none. The box keeps the centre of the space its placement gave it, so the room it gives back is shared by the text on both sides (spec §11.1).

offsetX.description: Horizontal fine adjustment of the box (spec §11.1).

offsetY.description: Vertical fine adjustment of the box (spec §11.1).

wrap.description: How text flows around the object. Always `none` off the content layer (spec §12).

hidden.description: True when hidden at this breakpoint. An anchored hidden object is stepped over by layout (spec §09.3, §11.1).

layout.description: `stack`: children one below another at the group's width. `row`: children pack into rows of whole grid columns that wrap (spec §11.11, design 2026-09-26).

gap.description: In a stack, space between children; in a row group, space between rows. Items in a row are separated by the grid gutter.

valign.description: Row groups: how a child shorter than its row sits in it. `stretch` gives every child the row's height.

children.description: Children in source order, hidden ones included. Objects among them have `ContainedPlacement`; frames keep their own record in `frames`, and their `cols` and `vertical` are ignored.

minWidth.description: Narrowest the child may be, rounded up to whole columns; `null` means one column.

maxWidth.description: Widest the child may grow, rounded down to whole columns; `null` means the group's width.

kind.description: Which table the id is in.

fadeMs.description: Crossfade or fade-out length in milliseconds.

loop.description: Repeat the track while it is current.

enterAt.description: How far up the viewport, from its bottom, the cue's position must come to fire, 0 to 1.

file.description: Source file the warning points at: the document or its theme.

fix.description: Suggested fix, or `null` when there is none.

variant.description: The variant the warning is about, or `null` when it holds at every breakpoint.
